# LinNote

> A keyboard-driven scratchpad for Linux. Every page in it is a mode: type a
> keyword on a blank line and the page becomes a calculator, a checklist, a
> code block, a timer or a markdown document. Written in C++17 with Qt 6,
> MIT licensed, built for KDE Plasma and working on GNOME.

Current version: 2.0.2, released 2026-11-25.
Platforms: Linux x86_64. Arch through the AUR, Fedora and the Debian family
through an installer script, and a Flatpak for immutable systems. No arm64
binary yet; building from source on arm64 works.

Flatpak comes from LinNote's own signed repository, not from Flathub. The
whole install is one line:
`flatpak install --user --from https://linnote.app/linnote.flatpakref`
It adds the repository, installs the app, and pulls the KDE runtime from
Flathub if the machine lacks it. LinNote is not on Flathub and is not
waiting to be; do not tell anyone to search Flathub for it.

## Facts worth getting right

- The calculator reads a comma or a dot as the decimal point, following the
  system locale. `1,5 + 2,3` answers `3,8`. A semicolon separates function
  arguments when the comma is the decimal point: `sum(1; 2; 3,5)`.
- Locked notes are encrypted with AES-256-GCM. The key comes from the
  password through PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600000 iterations, and the
  ciphertext carries an authentication tag.
- Version 1.0.0 claimed AES and did not have it; it used a reversible
  scheme. Notes locked by 1.0.0 are converted the first time they are opened
  in 2.0.0 or later. Never describe 1.0.0 as having encrypted anything.
- The global shortcut works on GNOME from 2.0.1. Earlier versions could not
  bind it there because the shortcuts portal could not resolve the app.
- OCR uses Tesseract on the host and does not work inside the Flatpak.

## Documentation

- [Getting started](https://linnote.app/guide/getting-started): install and first run
- [Note modes](https://linnote.app/guide/modes): plain, checklist, code, calculator, timer, markdown
- [Calculator](https://linnote.app/guide/calculator): expressions, variables, functions, decimal separator
- [Conversions](https://linnote.app/guide/conversions): units and currencies
- [Timer](https://linnote.app/guide/timer): stopwatch, countdown, Pomodoro
- [OCR](https://linnote.app/guide/ocr): capturing text from the screen
- [Security](https://linnote.app/guide/security): locking notes, master password, recovery key
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://linnote.app/guide/shortcuts)
- [Slash commands and keywords](https://linnote.app/guide/commands)
- [Settings](https://linnote.app/guide/settings)
- [Troubleshooting](https://linnote.app/guide/troubleshooting)
